LESSON: PAIRED READING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.1: Paired reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Paired reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is a good learner should be able to: pairs speed for reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. ask questions to confirm and extend procedure when supporting each understanding of material read other’s reading(making predictions
2. appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PAIRED READING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Paired reading helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PAIRED READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Ask questions to confirm and extend procedure when supporting each understanding of material read other’s reading(making predictions

What this means
In this part you learn to ask questions to confirm and extend procedure when supporting each understanding of material read other’s reading(making predictions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: ask questions to confirm and extend procedure when supporting each understanding of material read other’s reading(making predictions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Paired reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can ask questions to confirm and extend procedure when supporting each understanding of material read other’s reading(making predictions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Paired reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Paired reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Paired reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: ask questions to confirm and extend procedure when supporting each understanding of material read other’s reading(making predictions)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Paired reading to a partner. (skill: appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Paired reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: ask questions to confirm and extend procedure when supporting each understanding of material read other’s reading(making predictions.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Paired reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Paired reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Paired reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is a good learner should be able to: pairs speed for reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Paired reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: ask questions to confirm and extend procedure when supporting each understanding of material read other’s reading(making predictions.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
